verdict.rationale: Luma's Ray page documents transferring cinematic camera moves from a source video onto new scenes, worlds and styles. That gives creators first-party control over camera motion, but only by supplying reference footage, not by choosing named moves. Multi-Keyframe adds beat-level direction of what changes and what holds, though it is not stated to control the camera. missing for 10: named camera-move controls (pan, zoom, orbit, static) without a source video, documentation of how camera direction is specified in prompts or the API, hands-on corroboration that directed camera moves are followed.

support.subject: As a creator, I can direct camera moves (pan, zoom, orbit, static) instead of accepting whatever motion the model picks

citations.quote: Transfer cinematic camera moves across scenes, worlds, and styles.
Apply motion from a source video to new subjects, scenes, or styles.
